| [CLAIM-580](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-580.md) v2 | Transition threshold is stable under error | The assistant's own proposition, offered at the owner's invitation on 2026-11-05. The threshold of [CLAIM-571](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-571.md) is the least, over admissible paths, of each path's peak requirement, and both the peak and the least move by at most the largest error in the requirement. So a planner who knows each configuration's cost to within ε knows a transition's threshold to within ε, and its reconfiguration slack to within 2ε. The error is also one-sided in a useful way: overestimating only raises the threshold, and underestimating anywhere can only lower it, possibly by opening a cheaper path that does not exist. It is the zero-dimensional case of the stability of sublevel-set persistence that Mirth et al. use. With several resources the same argument bounds the set of sufficient budgets coordinate by coordinate. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [CLAIM-581](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-581.md) v5 | Transition threshold is a pseudo-ultrametric | The assistant's own proposition, filed on 2026-11-05 at the owner's invitation to contribute. Take configurations joined by reversible moves, each move with a peak requirement, and let d(x, y) be the least, over paths, of the largest requirement on the path ([CLAIM-571](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-571.md)'s threshold, identities free). Concatenating a path from x to y with one from y to z has peak max(d(x, y), d(y, z)), so d(x, z) ≤ max(d(x, y), d(y, z)): d is an extended pseudo-ultrametric (distinct states joined at no cost are at distance 0, unjoined ones at ∞; it is an ultrametric only when every pair of distinct states is separated by a positive cost). Hence at each budget b, "x and y can be turned into one another within b" is an equivalence relation, its classes are the components of the budget-b move graph, and as b grows the classes only merge, forming one dendrogram, the merge tree of zero-dimensional sublevel persistence (Mirth et al.). Under additive costs d is a metric and budgeted identification is intransitive in general. So which resource semantics governs a system decides whether "the same thing, within budget" sorts its configurations into a hierarchy of kinds at all. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
